report: full production security audit of the RUCHI Next.js + Supabase app
head: da4a6b4
methodology: Cloudflare security-audit-skill; architecture map → coverage-led hunting → validation → classification → severity → verification

findings.title: check-now carries a product-specific status that leaks enrollment state
findings.source_evidence: POST handler returns { ok: true, outcome: "not_opted_in" } when the caller has no prefs row; the store/UI treats that as the authenticated guest-message path. The endpoint does not 401 cleanly when the session is missing or the token is invalid — it falls through the token check into a 503 "service-unconfigured" or a silent no-op.
findings.attack_path: An unauthenticated caller sending any POST to /api/notifications/check-now receives 503 or a no-op rather than a uniform 401; a caller whose token Supabase rejects yields 401 only if the Authorization header is present. There is no single standardized 401 contract.
findings.impact: Low — inconsistent 401 behavior on one endpoint; does not expose data or bypass RLS. It weakens observability and lets unauthenticated probes receive product-grounded feedback instead of a clean denial.
findings.remediation: Return the same generic 401/403 for missing/malformed/invalid tokens across all /api routes; keep RLS as the ownership boundary. Make enrollment-state responses standard 404/409 without product meaning.

findings.title: deep-link landed used by notifications is read only in the browser and not enforced server-side
findings.source_evidence: URL params (?n=, ?recipe=, ?resume=, ?category=) are read client-side on mount and drive routing/targeting; there is no server-side validation that the URL target matches the user's session or the notification's own destination. The engagement RPC is RLS-secured, but the deep-link state machine is purely client-side.
findings.attack_path: A token-holder could open a crafted URL to pre-select a screen or pass a ledger id; the RPC still enforces own-row ownership. Whether a crafted URL can influence behavior beyond navigation is unverified locally because hosted Supabase is unreachable in this environment.
findings.impact: Unresolved — depends on reachability of hosted Supabase and on whether the URL is ever processed outside the browser (e.g., native shell, SSR).
findings.remediation: Keep deep-link handling read-only for navigation; rely on the RLS-secured RPC for any ledger mutation; treat URL-derived screen routing as client-side convenience, not a security boundary.

findings.title: production fire of the notification cron has never run against hosted Supabase in this execution network
findings.source_evidence: vercel.json schedules /api/notifications/run at 12:30 UTC daily; the route is service-role + CRON_SECRET gated and the pipeline is deterministic. The live end-to-end loop (delivered → opened) cannot be executed from this network because hosted Supabase REST is unreachable at execution time; the repo's own E2E simulation runs against local Postgres with the same RLS semantics.
findings.attack_path: Without a live cron fire, the delivery → opened chain is unverified in production. The schema/test suite and code review establish the boundaries, but a network-level blocker prevented live confirmation.
findings.impact: Unresolved — a platform/environment limitation, not a code defect. Needs a reachable-network cron fire or an explicit synthetic-subscription verification decision.
findings.remediation: Re-run the cron from a reachable network, or explicitly accept synthetic-subscription verification; add a CI health check that reports prod route status as environment health, not code.

findings.title: device push subscription not persisted server-side for the user's account
findings.source_evidence: subscribe route stores web_push_subscription in the user's own row; the existing deployment still shows notification_prefs.web_push=false and no live subscription exists for the account. The client push path uses the public VAPID key only.
findings.attack_path: Without a live subscription, delivery cannot be verified; the "sent→opened" chain remains unverified. Risk of untested integration is documented as environment-blocked rather than a code fault.
findings.impact: Unresolved — requires a real browser/device to complete verification.
findings.remediation: Complete device opt-in on a reachable device; if not possible, explicitly accept synthetic-subscription verification, or document the delivery gap as an operational blocker.

findings.title: AI/LLM front-end contracts (Gemini, recommendation, cooking assistant) are not production-enabled
findings.source_evidence: getRecommendationService and getAssistantService resolve null (deterministic fallback); aiConfigured() returns false; the AI layer is provider-agnostic only. Risk classification within this codebase: no live LLM surface to attack.
findings.attack_path: No production AI path exists to probe for prompt injection, tool abuse, or secret exposure. All AI flows degrade to deterministic fallbacks.
findings.impact: Unresolved — no live AI attack surface in the current product state.
findings.remediation: When the AI surface is enabled, add output validation and tool authorization at the final action boundary; treat absent AI as not-a-vulnerability.

findings.title: Android shell architecture not yet implemented; no source changes required
findings.source_evidence: Capacitor 8.5.2 Android shell loads the remote URL; no native deep-link handling, native push (FCM/APNs), or native camera plugin present. Build-verified (gradlew clean assembleDebug).
findings.attack_path: The shell is not deployed and is not part of the audit scope; the web app remains the security boundary. Native bridges are future work and do not weaken the current stack.
findings.impact: Unresolved — no Android code path exists for an attacker to reach.
findings.remediation: When Android ships, add native bridges behind RLS and keep web-safe patterns; this is out of scope for the code audit and requires a shipping decision.

findings.title: CSP allows blob: data URI, but the app has no exploitable blob rendering
findings.affected_component: src/app/globals.css + img-src blob: in next.config.ts CSP
findings.source_evidence: CSP is conservative: frame-ancestors none, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, strict-origin-when-cross-origin, camera/mic/geolocation/payment/usb gated, connect-src allows only Supabase. img-src includes data: and blob: for the camera flow.
findings.attack_path: No client code renders user-controlled content to ; uploaded images are not stored; fonts/dynamic styles are limited to self+data. blob: does not create an XSS path here.
findings.impact: Rejected — no credible attack path; the header is appropriate.

findings.title: Vercel route probe semantics are a probe artifact, not a vulnerability
findings.source_evidence: GET on POST-only routes returns 405; probes that issued GET reported 405 while POST worked. This is expected HTTP method semantics; the documented probes were POST (check-now/engagement/subscribe) and GET (run/vapid) and produced 401/200.
findings.attack_path: None. Method restriction is correct and enforced.
